title: Uniformity of the special coordinate under the disjoint-conditioned distribution
statement:
Fix $n \ge 1$, and consider the hard distribution on $\mathrm{HardSample}(n)$ conditioned on the disjointness event (that Alice's set $X$ and Bob's set $Y$ are disjoint). Then for every coordinate $i \in \{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, the conditional probability that the special coordinate $T$ equals $i$ is exactly
\[
\frac{1}{n}.
\]
In other words, conditioning on disjointness leaves the special coordinate $T$ uniformly distributed over the $n$ coordinates.
hypotheses_covered: the fixed coordinate i ∈ Fin n
measure is the hard distribution conditioned on the disjointness event
conclusion: real-valued probability of {T = i} equals 1/n
replaced: Under the disjoint-conditioned hard distribution, the special coordinate remains uniform.
